rationale: The Court is most likely to issue a narrow, unanimous opinion (probably by the Chief) cabining Rogers to titles/content of expressive works and holding that when the challenged use functions as a source identifier on goods, ordinary likelihood-of-confusion and dilution rules apply with parody considered within those frameworks. Separate writings are most likely from Justices inclined to emphasize textual limits in the dilution exclusions (Thomas/Gorsuch/Barrett) or to underscore speech/chilling-effect concerns while agreeing that the Lanham Act’s multifactor tests can accommodate parody (Alito/Sotomayor).
